name: Barnard's Star
description: Official test target. Highest proper-motion star in the sky (~10.4"/yr): ~1.9 SPHEREx pixels over the DR1+QR3 baseline (1.66 px measured offline on the FITS files between the Aug 2025 and Aug 2026 seasons). Saturated core: image brightness is not a measurement.

notes: Automatic detection and catalog matching were not run.

Pixel values and stretch limits are IMAGE - ZODI (SPHEREx zodiacal model subtracted) in MJy/sr; PNGs use an asinh mapping with the same contrast for every frame of a detector, and transparent pixels mean no data. Saturated star cores that SPHEREx left empty (NaN) and detector-defect pixels (NONFUNC, HOT, COLD, PERSIST, SNOWBALL, and SUR_ERROR that is not part of a star's profile, e.g. cosmic-ray hits) are filled from their neighbours for display only; SUR_ERROR pixels on a star and finite OVERFLOW pixels are shown as recorded. All of them count as invalid in valid_fraction. thumb.png is a D5 frame.

Frame selection: downloaded 80 candidate frame(s) (up to 2 x max_frames=40) and kept 40, spread round-robin over seasons x detectors; inside each (season, detector) the frames whose wavelength at the field centre is closest to a per-detector reference (D1 0.936 um, D2 1.517 um, D3 1.793 um, D4 3.015 um, D5 4.296 um, D6 4.581 um) come first, then those nearest the season middle; frames without a known wavelength rank last. Rejected 0 bad frame(s) whose IMAGE - ZODI robust scatter exceeds 15x the noise of their VARIANCE plane (background steps) and 3x the median of the same detector's candidates (on bright nebulae every frame scatters more, so only outliers are rejected). Downloaded 61 more D2/D3 frame(s) only to find J/H/Ks wavelengths for the false-color composites; they are not blink frames.

Registration check: every frame's field stars were compared with their median position over the field's candidate frames (all detectors: a correct WCS puts a star at the same grid position at every wavelength); 77 of 80 blink candidate frame(s) and 57 of 61 J/H/Ks top-up frame(s) checked (kept: median 0.03 px, max 0.09 px); the other 7 had fewer than 3 field stars measurable to 0.15 px (e.g. around a saturated target) or too few frames for a consensus, and were kept unchecked.

False-color composites: 3 'detectors' and 3 'jhk' season composite(s) (infrared, not true color). detectors = full range: blue = D1 (fallback D2), green = D3 (D4), red = D6 (D5), coadds of the season's published frames. jhk = 2MASS-like: blue / green / red = coadd of the season's downloaded exposures (including unpublished candidates) within 0.06 µm of J 1.25 / H 1.65 / Ks 2.17 µm at the field centre, else the nearest one within 0.12 µm. Each channel: one weight per frame, sky removed, bad pixels left out; a pixel bad in every frame of a channel (saturated core, detector defect, ramp-fit error) is drawn neutral at the brightest channel's level, so saturated cores look white (display only). Green spans 2 sigma below the sky to the bright end of its usable pixels; red and blue are scaled to green by the median field-star flux ratio (target halo excluded), so typical bright field stars look white; limits shared by every season with the same detectors, except that a noisy channel (pixel noise above 3% of its range) has its black point set per season at its own sky + 2 sigma, so its speckle goes black (fainter field stars then look the complementary colour); colour-preserving asinh (Lupton et al. 2004).

Updated in place on 2026-11-15 23:57 UTC (WS2): false-color composites and provenance/composite notes regenerated with the current pipeline from the same frames (frame PNGs, frame metadata and frame_flags unchanged; built_at is the build time of those frames).
False color: SPHEREx infrared wavelengths mapped to red, green and blue (infrared, not true color).
Full range: red = D6 4.60 µm, green = D3 1.81 µm, blue = D1 0.94 µm (mean wavelength at the field centre).
Colour balance: red and blue scaled to green by the median flux ratio of the field stars (red x0.191, blue x0.873; median of 3 season fit(s)), so typical field stars look white.
Colours are relative to the field: typical bright field stars look roughly white and an object redder than they are looks red.
